debates.topic: Outpost-scale lunar construction: S4 timing, band and threshold (robo-lunar-construction)
debates.skeptic_view: S4 gets two years plus a band step on a launch-bound node, against the brief's credit of 0.5-1.5 years. The labor share is 0%, its 0.4-0.6x credit holds only with 10+ cargo landings a year, and hardware lands frozen. Move S4 to 2034 Low. Also, 1,000 m2 is smaller than one heavy-lander pad, so make the first robot-built pad a hard prerequisite and raise the threshold.
debates.advocate_view: Moon-mars dates real robot construction from 2032 and gives S4 High to the robot-built pad and to lunar oxygen. The work content is small, so landed mass and power bind, and those are High by 2035. Move S4 to 2032 High and S3 to 2034 Medium.
debates.resolution: Threshold raised to two heavy-lander pads plus berms and roads (about 10,000 m2), and the hard edge from auton-robotic-landing-pad added (skeptic). Years and bands kept at S4 2033 Medium and S3 2035 Low. On Earth-labor terms the skeptic's condition-1 objection holds, but on the Moon robots are the product: capability per landed kilogram is the throughput, and the S4 analysis gives 0.4-0.6x of S3's calendar if cargo reaches 10+ landings a year. The advocate's arithmetic, recomputed for the new threshold, shows power sets the pace. Grading takes about 150 days for 20 robots. Sintering two 50 m pads takes about 280 MWh: 4 months at 100 kW, or 1.5-2 years on 40 kW of daytime solar. That rules out 2032 High.

debates.topic: Robots at a quarter of aerospace production labor (robo-aerospace-labor-quarter)
debates.skeptic_view: The base path gives 24.92% in 2035 on supply alone (fleet x 0.5% allocation x 1.6 FTE per robot). Suppliers start only after 2031, at 6-24 months per process each, and most of the ~2M workforce builds commercial aircraft under FAA and EASA approvals. Move S4 to >2035 Low.
debates.advocate_view: A year is the first credible year. The fast path crosses 25% about 2033, so S4 should be 2033 and keep Medium. Add a supplier-tier node as a hard prerequisite.
debates.resolution: Skeptic on year and band: S4 >2035, Low. The supply-only figure is an upper bound, because requalification also slows how many robots aerospace takes up. The fast path (20% of S4's weight) carries the Low band. The advocate's supplier-tier node was added as a hard prerequisite: S4 2033, Medium by 2035. It makes the brief's rule that suppliers come after 2031 visible.

debates.topic: First credible year or base-path year for robot count and share nodes (fleet-10m, mfg-10pct, construction trades)
debates.skeptic_view: Not raised directly. The skeptic's general position is that S4 is already generous in 2029-33.
debates.advocate_view: The model says a year is the first credible year and the band carries the expectation. The fast path is 20% of S4, so fleet-10m should be 2031 and mfg-10pct 2034 Medium (about 0.39 chance by 2035). Construction trades should be 2031, since the base path puts 0.25M robots in construction that year.
debates.resolution: Rejected. The brief defines S4 by the base path and treats the fast path as upside, so years follow the base path and the bands carry the fast path (fleet-10m stays 2032, Low by 2031). For mfg-10pct, the fast path already is the upper tail. Adding a 35% within-base chance double-counts it, and about 30% is the fair estimate, so >2035 Low stays. The 2031 construction robots are mostly earthwork and handling, and trade work by 100,000 robots needs about a year after it becomes useful, so 2032 stays.

debates.topic: Order of the aerospace gates: requalification route, tolerance work and the 24/7 line

debates.advocate_view: The route's earliest date is 2029-30, and the brief dates inspection and handling to 2029. One robot on one task in 2028 can complete a 6-12 month requalification in 2029, so date the route 2029.
debates.resolution: Route to 2029 (advocate). That clears the shared year without delaying tolerance work, which stays at 2030, the early end of the brief's 2030-31. The 24/7 line stays at 2031, leaving a year for the rest of the line to be requalified in parallel. The skeptic's description fix was accepted: at least 1.15x over the same firm's crewed line. The skeptic's proposed hard edge from factory usefulness to the route was rejected. Requalifying one process at one site does not need 100,000 robots in multi-task work, so the link stays soft.

Repeated operation needs design about 2031, qualification, a first flight in 2033 and a repeat in 2034. Move S4 to 2034.
debates.advocate_view: Neighbors give S4 a step: the flight demo is High and the km-scale monolith is S4 2033. Orbital compute and MRV show demand. Move S4 to 2032 Medium.

It also shows a design built alongside the demo and 6-18 months of mechanism qualification, so 2033 survives the skeptic's own timeline. Medium was rejected: deployables, Starship's 9 m fairing, SpaceX's many-satellite approach and OSAM-1's cost keep demand uncertain. The 2-year S4 lead stands because the S4 analysis credits robotic assembly in space by 2035.

Bands should drop to Medium in S2-S4 and Low in S1.
debates.advocate_view: Mach33's reference tonnage passes 300 Starship flights a year around 2029-30. The Louisiana campus plans ten pads with first launches as soon as 2029. Going from 100 to 300 a year at 1.44x a year is slower than Falcon 9's ramp. So the years should be 2033/2032/2032/2032 and High in every scenario. AI moves the launch clock only by months, so the S1 two-year lag is too wide.

S2-S4 should rise to High once a launch-site review covering 300+ a year is filed. Years are kept. Mach33's reference has about 35,400 t, or 240-320 flights, in 2029 against 145 approved caps, so it ignores caps and cannot date the node. The only Louisiana filing is a reported construction permit (Sep 29 2026, unconfirmed). S1 lags because of weaker compute demand, while AI moves the clock by months.

debates.topic: Starship internal cost under $100/kg: year and heat-shield gate
debates.skeptic_view: The node's own why says $100/kg needs ships flying about 10 times and that this depends on the heat shield. That is a hard gate written as a soft edge. High by 2035 must not exceed the heat shield's band. SpaceX does not report cost per kg.
debates.advocate_view: The draft's arithmetic ($100M stack, 18 flights, $4M operations, 112 t) gives about $85/kg. Mach33's base reaches 18 flights per stack in 2030, and with a 0.85 learning rate the stack costs about $90-100M. Mach33 therefore crosses $100/kg in 2030, and the model's one-year lag gives 2031, not 2032.

Years become 2032/2031/2031/2031, and the heat shield becomes a hard prerequisite; it lands 2031/2030/2029, so no year is pushed later. band_2031 is L/L/M/M: S2 stays Low because the heat shield is only Medium by 2031 and the chain has no slack. band_2035 stays High in all four only while the entry branch keeps the heat shield High.

The realized ranges apply to programs run under that year's conditions. A program finished in 2033 ran on 2031-32 robots, at a realized 40-50%. The fix is to narrow the scope to vehicles and large spacecraft, with S3 2035 and S4 2034.
debates.advocate_view: The node needs one fast program at one leading firm. Satellite generations at 0.32-0.44x for leading S4 firms in 2035 already halve. The S2 ceiling of 42-52% passes 50%. So: S2 2035 Low, S3 2033 Medium, S4 2032 High, with a soft edge from satellite-gen-cadence.
debates.resolution: Skeptic accepted. The advocate's case confirms the overlap, since it rests on satellite generations. Narrowing gives the node a distinct meaning: program-level halving where the space-program Amdahl applies. With S4 at 2034 against S3 at 2035, and Medium against Low, S4 credit comes from robot-first integration and test on requalified processes.

debates.topic: Start-to-orbit in three years: derivative or clean-sheet base (physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit)
debates.skeptic_view: Applying clean-sheet multipliers to a 4-year derivative base counts the derivative shortcut twice. On the 5-13 year clean-sheet base, S3 gets 3.2 years at best, so S3 should be Low and S4 Medium. A 2033 orbit in S2 implies a 2030 start at 0.8-0.9x, which takes 3.2-3.6 years. About half of new launchers fail on their first flight.
debates.advocate_view: The node needs one program worldwide, and China alone has more than ten commercial firms with methalox engine families. The draft's own S3 range of 2.5-2.9 years sits wholly under 3, so S3 should be High and S2 Medium.
debates.resolution: Split decision. The S2 year moves from 2033 to 2035 and the timing is corrected: a program must start by 2032 and runs under 2032-35 conditions, giving 3.0-3.5 years in S2 and 2.6-3.0 in S3. The clean-sheet base is rejected because the node counts derivatives and a proportional multiplier on a shorter base does not count the shortcut twice. The advocate's raises are rejected because maiden-flight failures and pad access keep S3 at Medium. S4 keeps one band step to High: a robot-first program at 0.50-0.58x needs 2.0-2.3 years.

S3 cannot reach 10 GW by 2034, and S2 cannot reach it by 2035. Chips (about 2.9 million GPU packages) and the dawn-dusk payload penalty also bind.

debates.resolution: Skeptic accepted: S2 after 2035 (Speculative), S3/S4 2035 (Low). The Mach33 reference is verified, but it launches 108,000 t of compute in 2032, which is about 700-1,100 flights. That is roughly three times the 300 heavy flights a year the trunk first reaches in 2032-33, and this branch must follow the trunk's clock. The advocate's 'central' ramp uses the trunk's earliest (optimistic) years plus V4 payload and 100 kW/t together. A rough simulation over plausible ranges gives medians of 5-6 GW (S3) and 4-5 GW (S2) at end-2035. The Mach33 figures are recorded in the node status. If the trunk speeds up cadence, revisit.

debates.topic: Do general-purpose robots (S4) earn credit at the launch gate?
debates.skeptic_view: Launch binds and robots do not touch it. With the km-monolith credit removed, the branch has no S4 credit anywhere, which is the right result.
debates.advocate_view: The trunk promised S4 credit for robot-built pads 'on later build-outs', but no node carries it. Robot crews build pads and propellant plants from 2033 at 0.50-0.57x of the usual time. That adds 1.2-1.35x flights in 2034-35, so S4 makes 10 GW in every case and should be High.
debates.resolution: Mechanism accepted, magnitude rejected. A soft edge from robo-earth-pads-plants to 10 GW records the link. Pads started in 2033 finish in 2034-35, adding roughly 0.2-2 GW by end-2035 against a central S3 path of about 5-6 GW. That lifts S4 within Low but not to a band step. Airspace, approvals, SSO-capable Florida sites, chips and capital do not compress, and the advocate's S3 ramp (700 flights in 2035) runs above the trunk. S4 equals S3 on every node. The trunk resolver should fix its own note that points to a credit no node carries.

debates.topic: What is a kilogram saved worth on a compute satellite?
debates.skeptic_view: The draft argues both sides. It uses 'cadence capped' to raise arrays and 100 kW/t, and '$13/kg makes mass cheap' to hold radiators. The fix is to lower arrays in S2, drop the $13/kg clause and keep radiators Medium.
debates.advocate_view: When flights bind, a kg saved flies more compute, worth billions a year at 2-3 GW a year. Radiators should go to High in S2-S4 and 100 kW/t to High in S3/S4.
debates.resolution: One rule now applies to all mass levers: mass matters through flight count where flights bind, and flights bind growth past about 1 GW. That is likely by 2035 in S3/S4 and less so in S2. Arrays: S2 Medium, S3/S4 High. Radiators stay Medium everywhere. The cut is about 5% of mass per GW, hot chips (High by 2035) shrink radiator area and with it this lever, and arrays carry about six times the leverage per kg/m2. 100 kW/t stays Medium because it needs roughly twice AI1's array specific power plus hot chips together. The $13/kg and 'capped cadence' texts are removed.

debates.topic: Kilometre-scale monolith and the only S4 credit
debates.skeptic_view: s4-embodied credits '100-m-class assembly plausible by 2035', which says nothing about a 1 km node. The gate is capital, so S4 rule 1 fails. No program is funded and formation flying meets the need, so every scenario should be after 2035.
debates.advocate_view: Keep the one-year S4 credit with a new reason: robotic assembly at scale (2033) plus launch under $100/kg makes a km truss a question of capital.
debates.resolution: Skeptic accepted: after 2035 and Speculative in every scenario. A capital-gated node gets no S4 credit by rule. A 1 km structure has about 100 times the area of the 100 m class that robots reach by 2035, and nobody funds one while formation clusters work.

debates.topic: 1 GW in orbit by 2035 (base case)
debates.skeptic_view: Going from Low to High in four years, before any Starmind has flown and before the pre-registered signal (production above about 1,000 satellites a year), is premature. S1 cannot sit level with 'ten compute flights in a year'.
debates.advocate_view: No direct challenge. The advocate's thesis kept 1 GW High by 2035.
debates.resolution: S2 Medium, S3/S4 High, S1 Low. Launch has slack for 1 GW (about 400 compute flights in 2030-35 against 110-180 needed), so demand and execution bind. S2 moves to High when the production signpost is met.

debates.topic: When is a model trained in orbit?
debates.skeptic_view: No finding. The draft had S2 2033, S3 2032 and Medium by 2035, since ground sites may stay cheaper and labs may not disclose.
debates.advocate_view: 1e26 FLOP is about 100 satellites for a month, a few percent of the fleet. The 'largest runs' objection does not apply to this threshold. SpaceXAi runs both the fleet and a lab and has reason to announce, so S2 2032, S3 2031 and High by 2035 in S2-S4.
debates.resolution: Mostly accepted: S2 2032, S3/S4 2031 (Low by 2031), High by 2035 in S3/S4. S2 stays Medium because in S2 the fleet itself (1 GW) is only Medium by 2035.

debates.topic: Megawatt-class compute satellites
debates.skeptic_view: A 1 MW satellite is about 3-4x outside the filed FCC envelope, so it needs a modification (the Gen2 precedent took about 16 months). It also needs 4,000-6,000 m2 of array, and Starlink's size steps took 3-4 years. Move the years one later.
debates.advocate_view: Starlink mass grew about 1.34x a year. At that rate Starmind passes 1 MW about 2033, so the satellites should be High by 2035.
debates.resolution: Years move later (S2 2033, S3/S4 2032), and the band stays Medium. The trend extrapolation reaches 1 MW only about 2033, with no margin. SpaceX's stated architecture is ten-satellite clusters of 250 kW satellites, and no filing covers MW-class satellites.

debates.topic: Does the power-per-kilogram step wait for perovskites?
debates.skeptic_view: No finding.
debates.advocate_view: The node's definition accepts thin-film or thinned III-V cells, and the perovskite node's own strongest case says these can deliver the gain. The hard edge is stricter than the definition.
debates.resolution: Accepted. The perovskite edge becomes soft and a light-array hard edge is added. S2-S4 move to 2032, Medium by 2035, and S1 to 2035, Low.

debates.topic: New 2032-35 nodes: captive chip fab and robotic compute-module swaps
debates.skeptic_view: No proposal. Chips and packaging co-bind 10 GW and belong in its text.
debates.advocate_view: Add a Terafab-style captive fab node (10 million accelerators a year by 2032 in S2) and an S4-led robotic module-swap node (S4 2034).
debates.resolution: Both rejected. The fab is a terrestrial supply anchor outside the branch's space scope. A logic fab does not supply HBM or packaging, and by the advocate's own strongest case it changes the cost of 10 GW more than its date. Terafab is recorded in the 10 GW status and signpost (facts verified via 33FG). Module swaps rest on an adoption gate, which S4 rule 1 excludes, and on a servicing business no operator has signalled. Starlink's practice is to deorbit and replace, with annual generations.

debates.topic: S4 band credits on the 1 t/yr oxygen plant, robot-built pad and assembly flight demo
debates.skeptic_view: All three fail the four-condition rule. Their binding gates are landed mass, power, sintering physics, run hours, a flight slot and funding. Labor does not bind them. The oxygen credit rested on 10+ cargo landings a year, which no node models. The pad is built by specialized sintering machines, and the demo needs a host plus 2-4 years of flight qualification.
debates.advocate_view: Rewrite the notes so upkeep is the gate after 2031: about 9 anode swaps a year, regolith feed and dust cleaning for the oxygen plant, and grading and tending for the pad. General-purpose robots do that work from about 2032, and one or two cargo landings are enough.
debates.resolution: Skeptic. Medium to High needs more than 70%. General-purpose robots doing outpost work on the Moon are themselves only Medium in S4 by 2035, so they cannot lift these nodes that far. With 10,000 h anodes (High by 2035) swaps fall to about one a year. Upkeep inside a plant is specialized automation already in S3, and the robots branch now makes the pad a prerequisite of robot construction. S4 equals S3 on all three.

debates.topic: S4 year and band credit on 10 t/yr lunar oxygen
debates.skeptic_view: A buyer and plant funding bind, and one excavator covers the regolith feed. The plant is built on Earth, where robots reach suppliers only after 2031 and need 6-24 months of requalification. A 2033 landing freezes its design around 2031, before pilot run data exist.
debates.advocate_view: The robots branch should move robo-lunar-construction to S4 2032 so the credit passes rule 2. Failing that, keep the band credit and drop only the year to 2034.
debates.resolution: Skeptic. The robots final keeps robo-lunar-construction at S4 2033, and changing it is outside this branch. Condition 1 fails on demand and funding, so the band credit goes as well: 2034 and Low in S3 and S4.

debates.topic: Moon Base Phase 2 band by 2035
debates.skeptic_view: The draft held S1 and S2 at Medium because appropriations and slips do not compress. That reason applies equally to S3 and S4, so they should be Medium too. A child node rated High would sit above its hard prerequisite.
debates.advocate_view: The threshold is modest: tens of kW and one semi-habitable element. The 2025 executive order, the Moon-first pivots at NASA and SpaceX and routine heavy cargo justify High from S2 up.
debates.resolution: Medium in S1-S4. Both reviewers found the same inconsistency. The executive order and the Moon-first plans set targets and carry no appropriations. Flagships slip 2-7 years, and the 100 kWe reactor is Low by 2035. Crew-optional ops drops to Medium with the base.

debates.topic: A hundred robots on the Moon at once: where S4 belongs
debates.skeptic_view: S3 2031 is too early, since fewer than ten robots have ever worked on the Moon at once. The fabrication gate looks chosen to pass condition 1. Lunar units need new actuators, seals and thermal control, so terrestrial volume does not make them cheap. S4 High exceeds robo-lunar-construction. Make every scenario Medium.
debates.advocate_view: This is a spine node, and the S4 band step rests on the reviewed fleet-size argument. Add robo-aerospace-tolerance-work as an input and name the fleet in the thesis.
debates.resolution: Split decision. I accepted the skeptic's years (2032 in S3 and S4), the 20 kg threshold, the hard edge from the base and S4 Medium. I kept the fabrication gate, because the metric is the robot count and 100 robots weigh 2-10 t, a fraction of one landing. I also lowered S2 and S3 to Low, which neither reviewer proposed. On the S4 base path the S4 analysis puts off-Earth robots at tens in 2031 and hundreds by 2035, and then only with ten cargo landings a year. robo-lunar-construction is Low in S3. This is the one S4 credit left in the branch.

debates.topic: Unmodeled lunar landed-mass rate
debates.skeptic_view: No credit can rest on 10+ landings a year until a gate node exists for that rate.
debates.advocate_view: Add 'Ten heavy cargo landings on the Moon in one year' at S3 2032, Medium by 2035 in S2-S4, as an exogenous anchor with soft edges into the 2033-35 lunar outcomes.
debates.resolution: Added as the advocate proposed, with no S4 credit. I dropped robo-earth-pads-plants as an accelerator because it lands later than the node. The node makes the S4 analysis's condition visible, and no band currently depends on it.

debates.topic: Lunar power without fission
debates.skeptic_view: The 100 kWe reactor is Low by 2035 everywhere, so night power rests on ridge solar and storage. This keeps the long stay and the water pilot low.
debates.advocate_view: Add a node for 100 kW of continuous ridge-solar power at S3 2033, Medium by 2035, because the 2033-35 lunar spine needs it.
debates.resolution: Node rejected. The Moon base node already carries tens of kW of night-surviving ridge solar, which covers the 1 t/yr and 10 t/yr plants (under 30 kW) and a habitat. No node here strictly needs 100 kW. I accepted the text fix: chains now cite ridge solar from Moon Base Phase 2 instead of 2030 base power.

debates.topic: Do test-bound nodes converge between S2 and S3 by 2035?
debates.skeptic_view: Not contested.
debates.advocate_view: Anodes, certified contact simulation and certified assembly skills share S2/S3 gates. Every hard parent is High in S2 by 2035, and S2 cognition is abundant by 2033-35, so S2 should be High.
debates.resolution: Advocate. On anodes the draft's S2 reason, that the carbothermal route may draw the funding, applies equally to S3. Contact-sim acceptance runs through NASA-STD-7009, an existing named mechanism, so the 2035 cap allows High.

debates.topic: First water from polar ice
debates.skeptic_view: No extraction payload is funded. NASA ISRU payloads take about 5 years from selection to flight. Power must come by cable because fission is Low by 2035. S2 Medium needs funding before its own models exist, and the S1 lag is inconsistent.
debates.advocate_view: Extracting 1 t takes one lunar day (about 1.3 MWh). The draft adds a needless landing-to-extraction year, so every year should move one earlier.
debates.resolution: Both in part. The extraction year is folded into the landing year, but the 3-year lag after excavator design now covers funding, build and landing, so S2 2033 and S3 2032 stay. S1 moves to 2035 on the same lag, and S2 drops to Low.

debates.topic: Starship-scale Mars propellant plant by 2035
debates.skeptic_view: Only the Apr 2033 window works. The plant needs about 1 MW, about 1 t of water a day and a design frozen before any Mars ISRU data, plus a second landing near the first.
debates.advocate_view: No Mars band moves. Windows and landed power already bind.
debates.resolution: Skeptic. The plant moves to >2035 in every scenario and gets a hard edge from the second-precision-landing node. The other Mars nodes are unchanged except architecture close, which falls to Speculative because of the joint chance of its three hard parents.

debates.topic: Regulatory cap on crew-side fault diagnosis
debates.skeptic_view: Not contested. The draft capped it at Medium everywhere.
debates.advocate_view: NASA's EIMO framework names clinical AI as a target, which is a named mechanism in motion, so S3 and S4 should be High by 2035.
debates.resolution: Rejected. EIMO is a capability roadmap with no acceptance route for crew-facing diagnosis, and the ISS test report is unverified. Rating S3 above S2 on acceptance would also break the brief's rule that the institutional overlay applies equally to S2-S4.

debates.topic: S4 credit for AI-found sorbents and catalysts
debates.skeptic_view: Not contested.
debates.advocate_view: Qualification is throughput-bound, and general lab robots from 2030 tend many parallel thousand-hour rigs, so S4 should be High by 2035.
debates.resolution: Rejected. The S4 analysis finds that robots collapse synthesis but characterization then binds, and they add about 5 points to materials, which is not a band step. AI-run test stands are already in S3 (condition 4), and program acceptance binds.

debates.topic: Long crew stays and lunar crop harvests
debates.skeptic_view: A 90-day stay needs both Medium hard parents, a pressurized habitat beyond Phase 2, power through three nights and a ride home whose propellant is kept cold for 90 days. Low in S2-S4.
debates.advocate_view: Add robot-built berms as an accelerator.
debates.resolution: Skeptic on bands. The berm edge was not added because robo-lunar-construction lands later than the stay in every scenario. Crop harvests are unchanged apart from text.

debates.topic: Soft-edge direction around robot lunar construction
debates.skeptic_view: Edges from robo-lunar-construction into nodes dated earlier in every scenario carry S4 credit backward and form a loop with the pad.
debates.advocate_view: Two soft 2-cycles hide which node drives the credit. Remove them and route the pad's robot input through robo-foundation-models-field.
debates.resolution: Both accepted. Construction is now downstream of the fleet and of the cargo cadence.

debates.topic: ARIEL atmosphere census timing
debates.skeptic_view: ESA now lists a 2031 launch. About two years of survey puts population papers in 2034 in every scenario, and one more slip pushes them past 2035, so the band is Low. Drop '1,000' from the title.
debates.advocate_view: The launch is 2031, but fast analysis is an S3/S4 edge. Use S3/S4 2033, S2 2034 and S1 2035, keep Medium by 2035, and drop '1,000'.
debates.resolution: 2031 launch verified on ESA's page. S2-S4 are 2033 as the earliest credible date: spectra from early 2032, a few hundred planets by mid-2033, papers late 2033. S2 cognition is cheap by 2033 and photons bind, so S3 gains nothing over S2. S1 is 2034. Medium by 2035 in S2-S4, because a 1-year slip still lands inside the horizon and only a 2-year slip moves it out. S1 is Low. Title changed. No ARIEL launch anchor was added, because the description also admits other surveys.

debates.topic: Heliophysics constellation flight
debates.skeptic_view: Multi-spacecraft missions take 6-7 years from selection to launch (PUNCH, HelioSwarm), and off-line viewpoints need 1-3 years of cruise (Vigil to L5). A 2030-31 selection returns 3D data in 2038-40. The S3 lead has no source.
debates.advocate_view: Add a robot soft edge for cheaper units, with no year credit.
debates.resolution: Skeptic accepted: >2035 and Speculative everywhere. The robot edge was declined because spacecraft cost is already carried by satellite-generation cadence and the gate is selection and budgets.

debates.topic: Satellite methane as compliance evidence by 2035
debates.skeptic_view: EU 2024/1787 names satellites for monitoring and super-emitter alerts, not compliance. Political risk is the same in S2 and S3, so the cap holds S2-S4 at Medium.
debates.advocate_view: The mechanism and the political risk are the same in S2 and S3, and both cognitive inputs are High by 2035, so S2 should rise to High along with S3.
debates.resolution: Both agreed S2 and S3 belong in the same band. The brief allows High only when a named mechanism already makes the path live. No mechanism yet makes satellite numbers compliance evidence, and the Commission has moved to 'pragmatic implementation' of the import rules (Dec 2025). So S2-S4 are Medium. Routine MRV follows one band below: Low, at S3 2033 and S2 2034.

debates.topic: Answer-first science missions
debates.skeptic_view: The onboard-inference input is 2029 in S2 and S3, so S3 has no lead. Explorers take 5-6 years from selection, and selections are scarce, so S2-S4 should be Low by 2035. The title nearly duplicates its prerequisite and uses a banned construction.
debates.advocate_view: Commercial and non-US constellations iterate yearly with no agency selection, so S3/S4 should be High.
debates.resolution: Years set to S2=S3=2033 and S1 >2035, with the new title. S3/S4 are Medium and S2 Low: the inputs share a year, but S3's input is High by 2031 and non-NASA agencies add chances. Commercial imaging services are excluded, because their onboard analytics is already under way and would redate the node.

debates.topic: S4 credit on a second private telescope
debates.skeptic_view: (Not reviewed. The skeptic's general point: robot edges must act before the node's year, and no science node gains S4 credit.)
debates.advocate_view: The private lane is the one place where builder throughput binds. A second telescope started in 2030 would meet all four S4 conditions and gain a year (S4 2032), with Medium by 2035 in S3/S4. Without it, 'S4 adds no year' holds only because no build after 2031 is modelled.
debates.resolution: The node was added, which answers the selection-bias point, but it gets no S4 credit. The funder decision comes first, and mirrors and detectors come from suppliers, who get robots after 2031. A 2030-33 build sits inside the 6-24 month requalification window. The S4 gate table gives leading firms about 15% on environmental qualification by 2031, which is 2-4 months on a 3-year build. Bands are Low in S2-S4 because no second funder is named. The thesis keeps 'S4 adds no year'.

debates.topic: Earth-twin radial-velocity detection
debates.skeptic_view: (Not reviewed.)
debates.advocate_view: The branch's biggest unlock for 2032-35. Separating stellar activity is statistics that cheap cognition attacks, and the Terra Hunting Experiment starts a 10-year survey in 2026. S3 2033, Medium.
debates.resolution: The node was added after checking the facts (ING page, DLR on PLATO), with years S3 2033 and S2 2034. It is Low by 2035 in S2-S4. Granulation and supergranulation set noise floors that only more nights reduce, seasons fix the cadence, and Earth-mass claims have a record of failing re-analysis. Data and seasons bind, so S4 equals S3.

debates.topic: Quantum sensor flight by 2035
